name: LightControl
author: LightControl Project
description: Grow-lamp LED panel and emitted-light control from the in-game phone. Color and brightness drive the lamp's own emitting LED panel and the light that lamp emits from the one resolved color, so both match. Emitted intensity is relative to the lamp's own native intensity, plant materials are never modified, and slot-scoped storage restores the original. Host/singleplayer placed grow lamps, on top of a game-independent light-control model.
manualTrigger: Open Light Control from the phone home screen. The graphite list has explicit Color, Brightness and ellipsis actions. Its 5x2 palette stages nine fixed colors or Rainbow: Apply confirms, Cancel/outside/phone close discards. Brightness steps apply immediately. More offers Original/Rainbow/Reset, immediate property copy and confirmed all-property copy. Inspect the one-shot [ui-layout] entries and compare the native view with ui-mockup.html. Escape closes the phone.
limitations: Native graphite UI acceptance remains open: compilation, policy tests and browser-reference measurements do not prove native rendering, font metrics, hit testing or gameplay. An owned 1201x655 reference canvas fits the measured phone; very small displays still need visual acceptance. Segoe UI uses the installed Il2CppStringArray overload with borrowed Arial fallback. Ten palette choices are nine fixed colors plus staged Rainbow; Original remains an action. Seven brightness steps apply immediately, with a 200-percent meter maximum. Original preserves intensity; Reset selects Original and 100 percent. Property/world copies include the source when applicable and reject stale target sets. Host/singleplayer control only, no client transport. Writes are limited to the lamp's owned panel clone and its own native light color/intensity; plant/world materials, switch state, transforms and other light properties are untouched. Regular LED and grow-tent halogen pairs only; FullSpectrum and the prologue RV are excluded. A lamp without both readable coupled outputs stays unavailable/pending, never forced on. Foreign materials are respected; unproven resource references may remain retained for later cleanup rather than being destroyed. Persistence keeps the existing schema and numeric slot identity, which does not distinguish another world/profile reusing the same slot/mod path. Unreadable storage and unresolved save-ID/schema conflicts block writes. Backup recovery requires full validation and protects the good backup from corrupt-primary rotation. Shared's normal writer uses temp/move plus best-effort backup, with no fsync/crash-durability guarantee. No free RGB, presets, custom names, new save schema, disco UI or localization binding. Default S1NoDeploy=true. See graphite-ui-verification.md for current evidence and audit-repair-verification.md for historical native/storage audit boundaries.
removal: Close the game, remove Mods/LightControl.dll. Optional metadata and symbols are in UserData/LightControl/. Keep lamps_slot-<n>.json to preserve settings, or delete those files only if you want to discard the saved lamp data.
